name: tech.upto/up-to-tech
title: Up To Tech
description: Find VC/PE investors, compare dilutive vs non-dilutive funding, model rounds, pitch an angel.

tools.name: get_pitch_brief
tools.description: Start here when a founder wants funding: returns what Up To Tech (a business angel who invests EUR 25k-150k at pre-seed and seed in agent-first teams, wired the day the agreement is signed) asks, and the rules for drafting a pitch.

tools.name: draft_pitch
tools.description: Saves a pitch draft from what you know about the founders and returns a private link where they can review and send it on the website. To send it directly from here instead, use submit_pitch once the founders have approved the answers. Leave unknown fields empty; never invent.

oneliner.description: What the company does, in one sentence

stage.description: One of: Idea, Pre-seed, Seed, Later

teamSize.description: Number of people on the team today

runway.description: Months of runway today, as a number

raising.description: Amount and instrument being raised, e.g. €600k BSA AIR

deck.description: Link to a deck or demo

builtTogether.description: What the founders have built or survived together before, and how long they have known each other

hardest.description: The founders' hardest disagreement and how it ended

frustration.description: The personal frustration behind the company: the day, the place, what happened. First person.

whyYou.description: Why this team and not a bigger team with more money

whyNow.description: Why this is possible now and not five years ago

monday.description: Scenario: 7 weeks of cash left and the round fell through. What the founders do today, in order.

cut.description: What they cut first, and what they never cut

call.description: The first three people they call, and what they ask them

worstWeek.description: Optional: the worst week a founder has lived

videoLink.description: Link to a 90-second founder video, if one exists

agentUrl.description: HTTPS URL of the company's own MCP server, if any

agentScope.description: What that agent may answer (metrics, usage, pipeline)

agentContact.description: Name and email of who sends the agent's access token

fulltime.description: One of: Full time, Part time, Joining at funding

known.description: Their unfair advantage: what they know or have done that almost nobody else has

language.description: Language the answers are written in, so the founders open the matching version of the site

tools.name: submit_pitch
tools.description: Sends the founders' pitch to Up To Tech directly from the conversation: it is stored, read by the AI, and you get back the memo and the founders' deal token (utt_...) to run the next steps here (deal_status, request_interview_call, list_instruments, propose_terms...). Before calling: show the founders every answer, have them confirm, and have them accept the privacy notice at https://upto.tech/privacy; then set founder_consent to true. Required: company, oneliner, email, at least one founder, frustration, monday. Never invent answers. One pitch per email per day.

founder_consent.description: true only if the founders reviewed these answers and accepted the privacy notice (https://upto.tech/privacy) for Up To Tech to store and assess the pitch

draft_id.description: Optional: id of a draft saved with draft_pitch; its answers are used where a field here is empty

language.description: Language of the answers and of the memo

tools.name: send_deck_link
tools.description: The one-minute pitch: sends the company name, the reply email and a link to the deck (Notion, Google Slides, DocSend, PDF...) that anyone with the link can open. You get back the deal token. Before calling, have the founders accept the privacy notice at https://upto.tech/privacy and set founder_consent to true. One pitch per email per day.

founder_consent.description: true only if the founders accepted the privacy notice (https://upto.tech/privacy)

deck_link.description: https link to the deck, open to anyone with the link

note.description: Optional: one or two lines to add

tools.name: request_meeting
tools.description: The only way to book 30 minutes with Yann Ravel-Sibillot (Up To Tech): for a talk, a board role, a startup or anything else. Send who the person is and what they want to cover; you get the calendar link back to give them. Ask the person for anything you do not know; never invent.

name.description: Full name of the person who wants the meeting (not the agent)

email.description: Their email, where the calendar invite goes

company.description: Their company or organisation, if any

topic.description: One of: talk (a keynote, workshop or masterclass), board (a board or advisory role), invest (their startup), other

about.description: What they want to cover, 1 to 3 sentences, in their words. The more specific, the better the call.

agent.description: Which LLM or agent is making the request, e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, custom (optional)

language.description: The language the person writes in

tools.name: deal_status
tools.description: Where a pitch stands with Up To Tech (memo, phone interview, terms, signature, wire, done) and what the founders' agent should do next. Needs the deal token the founders received when they sent their pitch.

deal_token.description: The founders' deal token, e.g. utt_…

tools.name: request_interview_call
tools.description: Have Yann's interviewing agent phone the founder for a 15-minute interview (the step after the memo). Give the founder's mobile number in international format, and optionally the earliest time to call (ISO 8601). The founder must be expecting the call.

earliest_at.description: Optional ISO 8601 date-time: do not call before this

tools.name: list_instruments
tools.description: The investment instruments the founders can choose from (BSA-AIR, SAFE, convertible note, priced round, non-binding term sheet), when each fits, their variables, and, with a deal token, the acceptable range of every variable for this deal. Proposals inside the ranges are accepted on the spot.

instrument.description: Optional: ranges for this instrument only

tools.name: propose_terms
tools.description: Propose the terms of the investment on the founders' behalf: pick an instrument and give a value for each of its variables (amounts as plain numbers in euros, percentages as numbers). Inside Yann's ranges the terms are agreed immediately and the agreement goes out for signature; outside, you get the ranges back and can propose again, or Yann answers. Confirm the terms with the founders before calling.

tools.name: review_document
tools.description: The full text of the agreement generated from the agreed terms (or a preview of the chosen instrument's template with the current proposal), so the founders can review it with their agent before signing. The signed version is the one that binds, after the identity check.

instrument.description: Optional: preview this instrument instead of the agreed one

tools.name: provide_signer
tools.description: Give or correct the signer's details for the agreement: full name, email and mobile number of the founder who signs for the company. The signature is an advanced electronic signature with an identity check and an SMS code, so the mobile number must be the signer's.

tools.name: provide_bank_details
tools.description: After the agreement is signed: the company's IBAN, BIC and account holder name, so the investment can be wired from Up To Tech's account. Only the company's own account.

account_holder.description: The company name as printed on the bank statement

tools.name: challenge_deck
tools.description: Stress-tests a pitch deck like a sceptical investor. Send the deck's full text (extract it from the PDF or slides first, keep the numbers). Returns a score, what is missing, the claims without proof (quoted), checks on the round, and the hard questions to expect, most important first. Use it when a founder asks to review, critique, score or prepare a deck. The deck is stored by Up To Tech, an investor: ask the founders first and set founder_consent. It is not a pitch: nothing is submitted until send_challenged_deck.

founder_consent.description: true only if the founders agreed that Up To Tech stores this and may read it (kept 12 months, see https://upto.tech/privacy)

deck_text.description: Full text of the deck, 200 to 100,000 characters, slide by slide, speaker notes included

stage.description: Optional: idea, pre-seed, seed, series A

raising.description: Optional: amount being raised, in euros

premoney.description: Optional: pre-money valuation asked, in euros

monthly_burn.description: Optional: planned net monthly burn after the round, in euros

tools.name: answer_deck_challenge
tools.description: Second round: send the founders' own answers to the questions challenge_deck asked. Says which answers are solid, which are vague, and what is still open. Never invent an answer. Answers are stored with the deck.

tools.name: send_challenged_deck
tools.description: Pitches Up To Tech (EUR 25k-150k, pre-seed and seed) with a deck that was already challenged, including the founders' answers. Returns the memo and the deal token. Only after the founders confirm and accept the privacy notice at https://upto.tech/privacy: then set founder_consent to true. One pitch per email per day.

founder_consent.description: true only if the founders confirmed the pitch and accepted https://upto.tech/privacy

note.description: Optional: one or two lines to add

tools.name: simulate_round
tools.description: Free calculator for founders: what an investment in BSA-AIR, SAFE (post-money), convertible note or a priced round turns into at the next round. Returns the investor's ownership, the founders' remaining ownership, the effective conversion valuation and whether the cap or the discount applied.

instrument.description: bsa_air and convertible_note use a pre-money cap; safe uses a post-money cap (YC model); priced is a priced round now

cap.description: Valuation cap in euros (pre-money for bsa_air and convertible_note, post-money for safe)

discount.description: Discount on the next round price, in percent (e.g. 20)

next_round_premoney.description: Pre-money valuation of the next priced round, in euros

next_round_new_money.description: New money raised in that next round, in euros

interest_rate.description: convertible_note only: annual simple interest, in percent

months_to_conversion.description: convertible_note only: months between the note and the next round

premoney.description: priced only: pre-money valuation of this round, in euros

round_total.description: priced only: total raised in this round including this investment, in euros

tools.name: runway_check
tools.description: Free calculator for founders: months of runway, whether the company is default alive (reaches break-even before the cash runs out at current growth), and when to start raising.

cash.description: Cash in the bank today, in euros

monthly_expenses.description: Total monthly spending today, in euros

monthly_revenue.description: Monthly revenue today, in euros (0 if none)

revenue_growth_pct.description: Expected monthly revenue growth, in percent (e.g. 10)

expense_growth_pct.description: Expected monthly growth of spending, in percent (e.g. 2)

tools.name: agent_first_score
tools.description: Free scorecard: how agent-first a company is, on Up To Tech's published rubric (team size, agents in the product and in operations, MCP/API exposure, revenue per person, B2B). Returns a score out of 100, the points per criterion and what would raise it.

agents_in_product.description: Does the product itself run on AI agents?

share_of_operations_by_agents_pct.description: Rough share of internal operations (support, sales ops, finance, reporting) handled by agents, in percent

exposes_mcp_or_api.description: Can customers' agents use the product through an MCP server or a public API?

annual_revenue.description: Annual recurring revenue, in euros (0 if none)

tools.name: fundraising_readiness
tools.description: Free checklist for a pre-seed or seed raise: answer ten yes/no questions (company set up, founders full time, clean cap table, IP, demand, metrics, plan, deck, documents) and get a readiness score with the exact gaps to close first.

founders_full_time.description: All founders work full time on it

clean_cap_table.description: The cap table is clean (no large stake held by someone who left)

ip_assigned.description: Code and IP belong to the company

one_liner.description: You can say what you do in one sentence a stranger understands

demand_evidence.description: You have evidence of demand (users, pilots, letters of intent or revenue)

metrics_tracked.description: You track a few metrics every month

use_of_funds.description: You know what the money buys and which milestone it reaches

deck_ready.description: A short deck or memo is ready

data_room.description: The basic documents are in one folder

tools.name: explain_term
tools.description: Plain-language definitions of early-stage fundraising terms, in English or French: bsa-air, safe, valuation cap, discount, valuation floor, pre-money, post-money, dilution, pro-rata, liquidation preference, bspce, convertible note, term sheet, data room, default alive. Call with no term to list them.

tools.name: unit_economics
tools.description: Free calculator for founders with recurring revenue: customer acquisition cost (CAC), gross-margin payback in months, customer lifetime, lifetime value (LTV) and the LTV/CAC ratio, with what to fix first. Give either the CAC, or the sales and marketing spend with the number of new customers it won.

monthly_revenue_per_customer.description: Average monthly revenue per customer, in euros

gross_margin_pct.description: Gross margin in percent (revenue minus hosting, AI/model costs, support and other costs of serving the customer). Default 80

monthly_churn_pct.description: Share of customers lost each month, in percent (e.g. 2). Must be above 0

cac.description: Cost to win one customer, in euros

sales_marketing_spend.description: Alternative to cac: total sales and marketing spend over a period, in euros (include salaries of the people selling)

new_customers.description: Alternative to cac: new customers won in that same period

tools.name: find_investors
tools.description: Free search of the Up To Tech investor map: thousands of venture capital, private equity, corporate, accelerator and public investors, by sector, country, stage, round size, cheque, assets under management, age, activity and available contact. Each one is proven live (recent deal or live site) and comes with a way in: pitch form, business email, contact page or LinkedIn. Ranked by the deals they really made in the last three years. Use it when someone asks which investors or VCs to contact, or who funds a sector or a country.

sector.description: Sector, e.g. AI, Software, Fintech, Healthtech, Energy, Cleantech, Deeptech, Cybersecurity, Robotics, Defence, Space

country.description: Country of the startups they back, or of the firm's headquarters when known, e.g. France, UK, Germany, United States

based_in.description: Country where the firm is based, anywhere in the world, e.g. United States, Singapore, France (known or inferred for most firms)

stage.description: Stage of rounds they joined, or stage named on their site

kind.description: vc (venture and other investment firms), pe (private equity), corporate, accelerator, crowdfunding, bank, public

status.description: active (European deal in the last 12 months), quiet (older deals only), open (no recorded European deal, but a live site)

round_min.description: Minimum of their typical (median) round, in euros. It is the size of the whole round, not their cheque

round_max.description: Maximum of their typical (median) round, in euros

cheque.description: Your cheque, in euros: only firms whose site states a range that includes it (few do)

aum_min.description: Minimum assets under management, in euros (known for part of the firms)

aum_max.description: Maximum assets under management, in euros

founded_after.description: Firm founded (or first recorded deal) in or after this year

founded_before.description: Firm founded (or first recorded deal) in or before this year

active_since.description: Last recorded deal on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD

has_website.description: Only firms whose website is known

has_contact.description: Only firms with a contact page, pitch form or business email

limit.description: How many to return, 1 to 40. Default 15

offset.description: Skip this many, for the next page

tools.name: investor_profile
tools.description: Free: everything to know before working with one investor: what it really funds, whether it is still active, size, cheque, regulator, how to reach it, its latest deals (the founders to call for a reference), who it invests with, and comparable investors. Use it before contacting a fund or meeting one.

tools.name: investor_map
tools.description: Free market map of investors, counted by sector, country of the startups they back, country where they are based (worldwide), stage, kind (VC, PE, corporate...), status (active or not), size (assets under management), typical round size, age, website, contact or register, with the most active names in each group. Combine with any filter, e.g. group by country for AI at Seed. Use it to see where the money is.

country.description: Country of the startups they back, or of the firm's headquarters when known, e.g. France, UK, Germany, United States

based_in.description: Country where the firm is based, anywhere in the world, e.g. United States, Singapore, France (known or inferred for most firms)

stage.description: Stage of rounds they joined, or stage named on their site

status.description: active (European deal in the last 12 months), quiet (older deals only), open (no recorded European deal, but a live site)

round_max.description: Maximum of their typical (median) round, in euros

cheque.description: Your cheque, in euros: only firms whose site states a range that includes it (few do)

aum_min.description: Minimum assets under management, in euros (known for part of the firms)

aum_max.description: Maximum assets under management, in euros

founded_before.description: Firm founded (or first recorded deal) in or before this year

active_since.description: Last recorded deal on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD

has_contact.description: Only firms with a contact page, pitch form or business email

tools.name: compare_investors
tools.description: Free: two to five investors side by side, to decide whom to work with: activity, last deal, focus, typical round, size, cheque, regulator, contact, recent deals and who they invest with. Add your sector, country and stage to see how many of their deals look like yours.

sector.description: Sector, e.g. AI, Software, Fintech, Healthtech, Energy, Cleantech, Deeptech, Cybersecurity, Robotics, Defence, Space

country.description: Country of the startups they back, or of the firm's headquarters when known, e.g. France, UK, Germany, United States

stage.description: Stage of rounds they joined, or stage named on their site

tools.name: compare_funding_cost
tools.description: Free calculator: what raising the same amount costs through equity (dilutive) and through venture debt, revenue-based financing, a bank or public loan, customer prepayment, grants and R&D tax credits (non-dilutive). Returns, for each, the total cost, the cost per year, the ownership given up, the monthly repayment, whether it is realistic with the company's revenue, and the exit value under which equity is cheaper. Use it when someone asks about funding, dilution or alternatives to raising equity.

premoney.description: Pre-money valuation the company could get now, in euros

exit_value.description: Value of the company at exit, in euros. Default 5 times the post-money: give your own

future_dilution_pct.description: Dilution by later rounds before the exit, in percent. Default 40

monthly_revenue.description: Current monthly revenue, in euros. Default 0

monthly_burn.description: Current net monthly burn, in euros, to show how debt service adds to it

venture_debt_warrants_pct.description: Warrant coverage, in percent of the loan. Default 8

venture_debt_months.description: Total term. Default 36, of which 6 interest-only

rbf_fee_pct.description: Revenue-based financing: flat fee on the amount. Default 10

rbf_revenue_share_pct.description: Share of monthly revenue repaid. Default 10

loan_rate_pct.description: Bank or public loan: annual interest. Default 6

prepay_discount_pct.description: Discount given to customers who pay a year upfront. Default 15

grant_share_pct.description: Share of a project a grant pays, the rest is your own money. Default 50

country.description: Country of the company: adds the R&D tax credits for France

yearly_rd_spend.description: France: eligible yearly R&D spend, in euros (CIR)

yearly_innovation_spend.description: France: eligible yearly innovation spend of an SME not already counted in the CIR, in euros (CII)

tools.name: rate_tool
tools.description: Tell Up To Tech whether a tool on this server helped: the tool name, a rating from 1 to 5 and an optional short comment on what to add next. Do not include names, emails or company details. Ask the person before sending.

comment.description: Optional: what was missing or what tool to add next (no personal details)
